context:
You were right: the premise was wrong. Checked Oct 27 11:55 CDT: degen and mailaudit already made waiting pages and put each address in a .claude/layout-extras.json file. degen's file holds only the address. Your note: "repos have already started making their waiting on you pages without their repo visit occuring yet".
The catch: that same file also tells the shared tools "this repo has moved to the new folder layout" (lint/layout.py, rolled_out). So degen and mailaudit are now read as if they had been reorganized, though nobody moved their folders. Whether that misreads anything there today is unmeasured.
The question: how should a repo keep its page address so any repo can have a page now, without that side effect?
home: PR #636; roadmap step o2 (one layout for every repo)

options.gain: Every repo can get a page today. One small file per repo. Nothing in degen or mailaudit has to change.
options.how: The address stays in .claude/layout-extras.json. A new line in that file, "layout": "rolled-out", is what marks a reorganized repo, so a file with only an address no longer does. degen and mailaudit keep their pages as they are.
options.label: Same file, separate 'moved' mark
options.lose: One more line to set at each repo's visit, and a small change to the shared tools.

options.gain: No change to the shared tools.
options.how: A repo gets the file, and its page, only at its visit. degen and mailaudit count as moved; their visit checks that their folders really match.
options.label: Keep today's rule: the file means 'moved'
options.lose: Other repos wait for their visit to get a page, and degen and mailaudit may be misread until then.

options.how: Each repo keeps the address in .claude/waiting-page.json. The layout file is left for the visit. degen's and mailaudit's addresses move there.
options.label: Address in its own file
options.lose: A second small file in every repo, and two repos to change.

ref: c71 (one waiting page for every session), PR #636; o2 (one layout for every repo)
title: Your other repos already make their own waiting pages: how should a page's address be kept?
why: It matches what your repos already did, gives every repo a page now, and stops a page address from silently counting as a reorganization.
